::: {.assignment-intro}
This project examines whether economic development across mainland China's provinces shows a cumulative “Matthew effect” or a movement toward regional convergence. It assembles provincial data on GDP, population, industrial structure, investment, urbanisation, education, and trade, then combines descriptive measures with panel regression and spatial analysis.

## Key findings

- Dispersion measures and the estimated relationship between initial income and subsequent growth support provincial convergence in GDP per capita.
- Industrial structure and trade openness help explain differences in provincial growth, while some controls are not statistically distinguishable from zero in the fitted model.
- Regional gaps remain substantial even as the longer-run national pattern points toward convergence.
- The animated provincial map and comparisons of representative provinces show that convergence can coexist with very different development paths.
